Detail: The pure policy starts only for lit renderer FULL with observable derived present:false, requests once at 30 seconds, resets on presence or observed dark-to-lit, and retries only failed sends after bounded backoff.

Title: LCUS-2 protocol, stable identity and latching-safe lifecycle
Detail: The standard-library POSIX transport opens the selected TTY at 9600 8N1, emits only the measured four-byte selected-channel commands, waits the measured settle interval, queries 0xff and accepts only a complete exact two-channel ASCII status. Lcus2Relay establishes OFF before ON, verifies ON heartbeats, never touches the other channel and opens a fresh transport to establish OFF when local state is absent. The udev rule maps measured CH340 VID/PID 1a86:7523 to /dev/wall-amp-relay. The daemon returns failure when shutdown OFF is unverified, and wall-sleep refuses S3 on that failure then reconciles the service after resume. The selector accepts lcus-2 alone: the audio-jack Tone, its trigger_out PCM and WALL_AMP_TONE_HZ are removed, and any other activator raises a configuration error so the daemon exits 78 instead of falling back.

Title: Door motion offline carriage credentials and power lifecycle
Detail: packages.list is the one offline dependency source and the artifact gate imports cv2 then executes the carried motion module in that installed closure. Capability validation refuses a shell missing doorstream/motion.py. Firstboot validates literal detector bytes without AWK escape reinterpretation, including at most 32 mask rectangles and 4096 ASCII bytes; defaults motion disabled and uncalibrated; and publishes a true effective enable only after both gates and all bounds pass. Purge first runtime-masks the unit against restart, then performs bounded stop, kill and reset handling and verifies both unit inactivity and no dedicated-account process throughout a stable settle interval before unlinking volatile state; inability to prove stable inactivity makes firstboot red and retains evidence fail closed. The service consumes only the exact root-owned credential allowlist without EnvironmentFile. Unit and shell time ceilings bound teardown; wall-sleep refuses backlight-off or suspend unless the fake-observable stop completes. SIM values are disabled, unreachable and property-neutral.

Detail: One module decides what the switch becomes and performs no I/O, so every Owner ruling is unit-testable without a sound card. normalize falls back field by field rather than discarding a damaged file. apply_event returns a journal line for every event including no-ops, refuses an unknown or malformed one, and never mutates its input. A presence report marked as coldplug is a fact and never an event: it records presence, sets the latch from what was seen (spent if the adapter was present across the boot, armed if it was absent) and never moves the position, so a power cycle comes back where the Owner left it whether or not the adapter was plugged in over the boot. plan is the single definition of which legs run, which cards are muted and what level is applied.

Title: Root applier, post-switch detector tap and the bus-mode chain
CodeSymbol: wall-audio-output.apply_plan; wall-audio-output.read_request; wall-audio-output.headset_card; wall-audio-output.save_state; wall-audio-output.is_boot_presence; wall-audio-output.headset_event; wall-audio-output.set_bus_level; wall-audio-output.probe_speaker_chain; wall-audio-output.select_speaker_chain; wall-audio-output.trim_command; wall-audio-output.load_trim; wall-audio-output.render_trim_conf; wall-headset-present.service; panel-amp-trigger.sources_for; asound-bus-mode.conf; wall-audio-mode.apply_bus; wall-spdif-in.service; wall-bus-speaker.service; wall-speaker-out.service; wall-bus-headset.service; wall-audio-state.service; wall-audio-apply.path; 91-wall-headset-adapter.rules
Detail: The applier is the only writer of the state file and the only caller of systemctl and amixer for the switch: it stops every leg that must not run before starting the one that must, mutes both cards around the change, and applies the level last because the softvol control does not exist until a PCM declaring it is open. The headset card is resolved from /proc/asound usbid on every apply, because the adapter enumerates under the generic id Device. Coldplug is told from a runtime plug by two gates over one monotonic clock: whether systemd reports the boot finished, which no slow boot can outrun and which replaces a dependency on udev settle, and whether this device's udev initialization time precedes the stamp apply-state samples when it begins and publishes when the apply lands. The device is dated through its sysfs card number, never through its ALSA id, which has no sysfs entry. Every doubt resolves to coldplug, the presence unit is ordered after the state unit, and apply-state refreshes presence without inventing a position. The softvol control is declared by the applier opening the leg's own PCM with no frames, and the remembered level set, before the forwarder starts, so a freshly created control is never exposed at full scale under running audio; the level is re-asserted last with a bounded retry. A mode switch starts every unit the bus graph needs, including the ones it stopped that were running but not enabled. Requests are deduplicated on a sequence recorded in the same atomic write as the change it caused, and a presence claim from the renderer is refused. Outside bus mode the state is recorded and no hardware is touched, so the switch can be set while the old chain is live. The detector's bus-mode source list is the post-switch tap alone and the actuator carries no mode branch, so leaving Speaker expires through the ordinary hold-off. Bus mode is additive and trigger mode remains a one-command rollback. In Speaker the leg opens the adapter's eight-channel altsetting and a route copies front through unchanged and an equal sum of both inputs to the centre and the LFE channels, with the remaining channels written as explicit zeros because the rear pair is wired to a desktop input. The route and its six coefficients are generated into a file of their own and are moved by a trim subcommand rather than by editing ALSA syntax: a refused coefficient moves nothing at all, a damaged file falls back coefficient by coefficient, and the command restarts the leg only if it is already running, counting an unanswerable systemctl as not running so that moving a number can never start audio. The up-mix sits below the volume control, so one control still moves every channel, and above nothing the detector reads, so the tap is untouched. The chain is chosen by one probe that opens it with no frames before anything else opens the leg, answering both an adapter without the altsetting and an absent trim file, and the answer is published to the unit and placed in the applier's own environment so that its pre-open cannot declare the control on a chain the leg will not use; the trim file is loaded by a hook that tolerates its absence, so a missing file costs the centre and sub rather than the whole configuration. The trim command runs under the same exclusive lock every other writer takes and restarts the leg only when it is running and the stored position is the speaker one, so a trim cannot revive a leg an apply has just stopped. A measured burst of boot-minute underruns is answered by a larger forwarder ring on the half that underran rather than by unit ordering, which would deadlock the first boot because provisioning is itself what starts the leg.

Title: Broker switch verbs, switch status block and method-aware reconciliation
CodeSymbol: routing.validate_action; routing.SWITCH_OUTPUTS; routing.switch_only_authorization; audio_router.AudioBroker._reconcile; audio_router.AudioBroker._safe_switch; audio_router.AudioBroker._without_seq; audio_router.serve; switch_request.envelope; switch_request.write; switch_request.next_seq; switch_backend.SwitchApplierBackend; switch_backend.backend_from_environment
Detail: set_output generalizes set_mute to the three-position switch and set_input_mute carries the separate microphone button; both take no alias, so a Bluetooth device alias can never reach the host switch and select_output remains a different verb with a different meaning. The optional status.switch block is validated against an exact positive schema and is what renders the red icon when the selected output is unavailable. Reconciliation is method-aware: a lost set_output is settled only by the switch block, never by the mute control, because a three-position switch is not a boolean. switch_request serializes one validated, sequenced request atomically into the broker's own runtime directory, which is how a service with no write access to /etc and no systemd socket reaches the root applier. The shipped backend is that writer: it answers set_output, set_input_mute, set_volume and the legacy set_mute, and nothing else, so the routed-device backend stays unimplemented and every alias verb is still refused. set_volume is self-reconciling on the switch block like the other two, is bounded rather than clamped at the broker, and accepts an optional output guard that refuses the request when the host switch has already moved, because the wire to the applier names no output and a level applies to whichever position is selected when it runs. The state file is normalized field by field exactly as the applier normalizes it, so a sparse file reports the position the applier will act on rather than an unknown switch, and reconciliation is not refused on a panel whose switch works. A mutation refuses when that file is present but unreadable, because the sequence floor, the volume guard and the legacy unmute are all decided from it and reading it as empty would mint below the recorded mark and acknowledge an unmute that never happened; status alone keeps the lenient read and reports the switch unsupported. The sequence is minted in microseconds and floored above both the applier's recorded high-water mark and any request not yet consumed, so it is strictly increasing across a broker restart, across two requests inside one tick and across a clock stepped backwards, and it stays inside the JavaScript-safe range the shell compares it in. A completed mutation is replayed from the journal only while its effect is still in force: the request file lives in a runtime directory the journal outlives, so a broker restart between the write and the applier consuming it would otherwise replay an acknowledgement for a switch that never moved, and the request is dispatched again instead, which is safe because every switch verb is idempotent and which neither advances the generation a second time nor treats the retry as stale. The sequence is returned in the reply only to a client that set echoSeq, which keeps the historic result shape intact for a shell that validates it as an exact key set. Authorization ships allowing the switch verbs alone: they name no device and are the physical control of the wall in front of whoever is standing at it, while Bluetooth authority keeps its deny-by-default.

Title: Mic leg graph, knobs and the applier half
CodeSymbol: wall_audio_state.mic_source; wall_audio_state.mic_live; wall_audio_state.MIC_LEGS; wall-audio-output.load_mic; wall-audio-output.render_mic_conf; wall-audio-output.parse_mic_assignments; wall-audio-output.parse_adapter_levels; wall-audio-output.rear_levels; wall-audio-output.set_rear_level; wall-audio-output.select_mic_source; wall-audio-output.rear_mic_possible; wall-audio-output.mic_command; asound-bus-mode.conf; wall-mic-rear.service
Detail: The switch position chooses the microphone, so there is no fourth control: the built-in capture in speaker and in mute, the headset adapter's in headset. Mute is an output position and ALSO mutes the microphone, by Owner item J 2026-09-14, which supersedes Owner ruling E: normalize() latches input_muted whenever output is mute, so an independent unmute cannot bypass the coupling, and the latched state is retained on a later route change until an explicit microphone-unmute; a headset selected with no adapter routes nothing at all, by Owner ruling 7, because falling back to the microphone in the room would be the one failure here with no audible symptom. The input mute stops both forwarders and closes every capture switch that exists, which is what makes it a real mute rather than something drawn over a running microphone, and the selected source is journaled on every apply so the difference is answerable from the journal alone. The adapter's single eight-channel playback stream becomes a direct mixing plugin so the speaker route and the mic route can share it; each is generated with an explicit zero in every channel it does not own, and that pair is the whole of the separation, because the card's playback mute is one boolean over all eight channels and cannot express front off with rear on. The rear pair's hardware level is read, modified and written back so the other six values, which are the Owner's bench work, are never guessed at; a read that does not answer eight integers moves nothing. That level is raised only while a leg runs and returned to silence otherwise, so two independent things must be wrong before the room's audio reaches the desktop. The selection is published before anything opens a microphone and placed in the applier's own environment, because ALSA resolves the name when the stream is opened and a forwarder already running would otherwise keep the microphone it started with through a switch change. A changed selection therefore restarts the legs. The leg is refused, with a journal line naming the fix, while the speaker chain has fallen back to its exclusive stereo open, because that path holds the adapter outside the shared plugin. No mic leg failure is counted against an apply: that apply runs under a unit provisioning waits on, and a microphone that will not start is a degraded panel, not a broken one. The knobs are a generated pair of files moved by a subcommand, refusing rather than clamping, moving the whole table or none of it, and restarting the leg only if it is already running.

Title: HFP mic return supervisor and the Bluetooth profile it needs
CodeSymbol: wall-bt-mic.parse_sco_sinks; wall-bt-mic.decide; wall-bt-mic.loop_argv; wall-bt-mic.read_sinks; wall-bt-mic.poll_seconds; wall-bt-mic.bus_mode_active; wall-bt-mic.Leg; wall-bt-mic.service; wall-bluealsa-override.conf
Detail: A synchronous-connection audio stream exists only while a call is up and is named after the phone's address, so there is no device node for a unit to bind to and this leg is a supervisor with a bounded poll rather than a forwarder unit. It reads the Bluetooth audio daemon's own object tree and runs exactly one forwarder for exactly as long as a playback endpoint is there. Only a playback endpoint counts: the capture direction is the far end's voice and is not this leg, and an advanced-audio endpoint is music rather than a call. A call in progress is never moved to another device, and the choice among several is deterministic rather than arbitrary so it cannot change between polls. Every failure to read -- a daemon that is not running, a missing tool, a slow bus -- answers 'no call', because the failure direction that matters is a microphone that stays open. The poll interval is clamped rather than refused, since no operator is standing in front of this process, and the loop sleeps in short slices so a stop is answered promptly. Leaving bus mode stops the leg, so the one-command rollback is not missing a piece. The profile is the hands-free role, which makes the panel the phone's headset as the specification asks, and not the gateway role, which is that relationship inverted; the advanced-audio sink is kept alongside it. Enabling a profile routes nothing on its own, and a device paired before it existed must reconnect before an endpoint appears. That the link is mono and suspends music for the duration of a call is the Owner-accepted cost of review finding 4.

Title: Telemetry sampler core, collector service and the renderer run directory
CodeSymbol: panel_telemetry_core.sample; panel_telemetry_core.cpu_delta; panel_telemetry_core.rotate; panel-telemetry.py; wall-panel-telemetry.service; wall-firstboot.sh install_panel_telemetry
Detail: panel_telemetry_core.py is the pure decision half -- sensor inventory, counter-delta CPU, the unknown-until-valid rule, the rotation and cap arithmetic -- so it is testable with no sensors, no clock and no disk. panel-telemetry.py is the shell around it: the monotonic schedule, the JSONL writer, the renderer snapshot reader and the export. wall-firstboot.sh installs the unit, runs daemon-reload, enables and starts it, and installs the tmpfiles fragment for /run/wall-panel-renderer -- the unit was staged but never installed before 49b0703, so step 8e failed on every run while reporting nothing.

Title: ProjectM preset payload reproduction from a committed lock
Detail: The builder runs in two modes: --refresh fetches a named upstream revision on a networked machine and writes the lock with a SHA-256 per file; every later run reproduces from that lock and fails on any missing file or hash mismatch. The lock is empty today and the builder says so explicitly and exits zero, which is the deliberate unruled state, NOT an install. NO INSTALL TRANSACTION EXISTS YET: nothing in wall-firstboot.sh or user-data stages or copies the payload, so the location the README documents is aspirational. That gap is open and belongs to the D release lane.

Title: Panel-local access store survives every deployment lane and apply script
Detail: The panel-local access store - the PIN record and the face enrollment - is durable user state, not deployed content, and every path that writes the panel must leave it alone: the release lane, a full reimage upgrade-in-place, a system payload activation, and any one-off apply or migration script run by hand under sudo. The HomeHub release lane already names the store file and its key in its PRESERVED list; this requirement extends the same rule to the lanes and scripts that had no such list, which is how the 2026-09-14 local-capabilities apply script came to set the PIN to null by design and silently remove settings saving, face unlock and attention configuration with it. A script that must nevertheless change the store states it in its own output and prints a wall-facing follow-up sentence, and no script may treat a missing or unreadable store as licence to recreate an empty one. Verified by reading the store generation and hasPin before and after each lane.

Title: Door broker lifecycle refusals are logged, never silent
Detail: The display lifecycle owns the Door broker, so every exit from its two helpers must be readable in the system journal after the fact. start_door_broker keeps its guards unchanged - an absent unit and unreadable /run/wall-door-credentials/{host,password} still start nothing, because display-on must never resurrect an older source - but each refusal now writes a warning naming the condition and the remedy, and a successful start is logged, and a failed systemctl start is logged AND still returns non-zero, because backlight_set has its own caller-side warning for that case and swallowing the status would hide the condition twice; only the two policy guards (no unit, no readable credentials) return success, since in those cases there is deliberately nothing to start. stop_door_stream logs a completed stop and warns on a stop that does not finish inside its ceiling. Credential FILE NAMES may be logged; credential VALUES never are, and nothing in either helper reads one. Rationale: on 2026-09-14 a credential purge followed by a wake left the broker down with nothing in the journal connecting the two, and the panel could observe only an absent listener.

Title: Face model bundle is staged whenever any camera-related option is configured
Detail: Item M, 2026-09-15 Owner ruling: the InsightFace buffalo_l face model bundle (det_10g.onnx, w600k_r50.onnx) is a dependency of any camera-related option, not a separate optional package. wall_camera_option_configured is duplicated by hand in vmtest/lib/common.sh (build time, reads the staged deploy-payload/site/wall.env) and wall-firstboot.sh (boot time, reads the panel's own wall.env): true when WALL_ACCESS_MODE=local, WALL_CAMERA_ENABLED is true/TRUE/yes/1, or WALL_CAMERA_DEVICE is explicitly set. At build time stage_wall_sensors_into_payload verifies a WALL_SENSOR_MODELS local input against the reviewed committed stack/autoinstall/wall/sensor-models/manifest.json with check-sensor-models.py (byte-identical manifest plus a matching sha256 per file, the same authenticity-anchor pattern check-wheelhouse-lock.py --expect uses for the wheelhouse) and fails the build with a named remediation when the predicate is true and no bundle was supplied; an unconfigured camera leaves an absent bundle a non-error. At boot time wall-firstboot.sh mirrors the same rule as a fail_step against /opt/wall-panel/sensor-models, alongside the existing SENSOR_WHEELHOUSE fail_step.

Title: Touch witness lifecycle and identity-based input node selection
CodeSymbol: wall-local-setup.py touch_identity; select_input_device; TouchWitness.resolve; TouchWitness.run; start_touch_witness
Detail: The root-owned evdev witness runs as a daemon thread of wall-local-setup.py - the process that already owns the wake socket and the power command - so touch wake adds no second privileged process and no new path from the kiosk account to power. It resolves its input node BY IDENTITY and never by an eventN path: node numbers are allocation-order dependent and change on every daemon restart and USB re-enumeration. The touch filter daemon holds EVIOCGRAB on the physical node in filter and adaptive mode, and the grab is exclusive - a second reader of that node opens successfully and then receives nothing for ever. Only FILTER mode creates a uinput device, though: configure-touch-filter.sh modprobes uinput for filter alone because adaptive's accepted taps leave over its AF_UNIX bridge to the kiosk rather than through a virtual device, so treating adaptive as a virtual-node mode made the witness hunt for a device that is never created and retry touch-node-missing for ever. The candidate list is therefore the virtual node then the physical node in filter mode, and the physical node alone in adaptive, shadow and off. Which candidate is USABLE is never decided from the persisted mode, which states intent rather than observing the live grab: the witness probes each physical candidate by taking EVIOCGRAB and immediately giving it back - one pair of ioctls, at resolution time only, never per contact, and never on the virtual node, which nobody can grab by construction - so a panel whose filter daemon is down or restarting falls back to the raw node and keeps waking, and returns to the virtual node as soon as the daemon is back. A physical node that is genuinely grabbed with no virtual node to fall back to (adaptive in its steady state) is reported once on a long backoff rather than retried every second. Zero matches or more than one refuses, exactly as touchfilter's own select_device refuses ambiguity, and every handle the enumeration opens is closed on every path except the one returned - a node can vanish between list_devices and InputDevice, and leaking the handles opened before that point ends in EMFILE on a loop that re-resolves every second. The honest cost, recorded rather than glossed: in filter mode the witness observes the FILTERED contact, so a contact the filter classifies as a fault is deliberately not a wake and a healthy filter is a precondition of touch wake; the witness journals the node class it resolved at startup and on every re-resolution so a wedged daemon is diagnosable from journalctl alone. The node may vanish at any moment - the unit is Restart=always and the uinput node is destroyed and recreated with a new minor on each restart and across suspend - so ENODEV and EOF are normal, re-resolution is by identity on a 1 s backoff, and the witness never fails the helper.

Title: Brightness-zero and rate-limit preconditions for a touch wake
Detail: A contact wakes the panel only when every readable backlight reads zero. The predicate mirrors electron/display-lit.cjs displayLit() for the backlight half - integer files, max_brightness > 0, lit iff brightness > 0 - and the two sides are pinned by TC-911 here and TC-P-422 in the panel repo so they cannot drift. No readable backlight is NOT darkness: with no evidence the witness declines rather than guessing. A tap on a lit panel is ordinary input and belongs to the compositor and to host-attention.cjs, so the witness does nothing with it. One wake per CONTACT and not per frame: the trigger is BTN_TOUCH down, the single event at the head of a replayed tap. The rate limit is one wake per 2 s measured on CLOCK_MONOTONIC, the same clock the filter daemon pins with EVIOCSCLOCKID; 2 s is sized to one deliberate tap and is NOT measured, so it is recorded here as one constant a later measurement can change. THE RATE LIMIT IS ARMED BY A COMPLETED WAKE AND NEVER BY AN ATTEMPT: exit 75 means the arm declined because a power decision held the lock, any other non-zero means the backlight did not come on, and both leave the panel dark, so both leave the clock untouched. Arming on a failure would make the panel ignore the person's next two seconds of tapping while still dark, which is the very symptom the Owner reported.

Title: The witness seam in validate_wake, and the unchanged socket refusal
Detail: The process asking for power is never the process attesting that the evidence exists. The contact is observed by root, in root's own address space, from a kernel device node, so the touch wake is UNREQUESTABLE: there is no request, no peer and no parameter for an attacker with the kiosk account to forge, and Electron gains no touch claim. validate_wake keeps its existing first line exactly as it is for socket traffic and gains a keyword-only witness seam that accepts exactly {source: touch} and nothing else. Helper.request - the only caller reachable from the socket - never passes witness=True, so a socket peer sending a touch source is refused wake-request-invalid by the unchanged line, and a test asserts that refusal so the seam cannot be widened silently later. Both paths run the power command in one place, Helper.wake, differing only in the wall-sleep.sh arm they invoke.

Title: The touch-wake arm, its serialization against the decider, and the re-sleep rule
CodeSymbol: wall-sleep.sh touch-wake; power_lock_acquire; power_lock_release; backlight_lit; suspend_now
Detail: run_occupancy is a decide-THEN-act sequence: the decider says BACKLIGHT=off POWER=suspend, the backlight write lands, and only then does suspend_now run. A tap arriving inside that window ran touch-wake from a DIFFERENT process, cleared the absence clock and lit the screen, and the occupancy process - still holding a decision taken before the tap existed - then suspended a lit panel on a stale absence clock and took it off the LAN in front of the person who had just touched it. So the decide-and-act window and the whole touch-wake arm are serialized on one lock file with flock, nested acquisition is a no-op rather than a deadlock because run_occupancy calls suspend_now, and a tap that cannot get the lock within the wait is DECLINED with a journal line and a non-zero exit rather than served on a stale view - the witness then does not arm its rate limit and the next tap tries again. suspend_now takes a last look under that lock immediately before suspending: on the occupancy path only, a backlight that reads lit again or an absence clock that no longer matches the stamp taken after the decision aborts the suspend with a journal line naming which one changed. The scheduled 22:00 path passes no guard and is byte-for-byte unchanged, because it never claimed to dim anything. The re-check is also the ONLY guard on a box with no flock, where the lock degrades to a warning rather than to silence. The touch-wake arm CAPTURES backlight_set's status rather than discarding it, releases the lock, and then exits with that status after a journal line naming the failure: this script runs set -u and not set -e, so a discarded status would have made the arm exit 0 on a backlight that never came on, the witness would have read that as a completed wake and armed its rate limit against a panel that is still dark, and the journal would have reported a successful touch wake. backlight_set already reads the level back, so its non-zero is the strongest evidence in the script that nothing happened and must not be the one status thrown away. Beyond that, wall-sleep.sh gains one case arm, touch-wake, that does precisely what sensor-wake does - clear ABSENT_SINCE_FILE and backlight_set on - plus its usage string. The behaviour is identical; the separate arm exists so the acceptance journal shows witness, request, touch-wake and restore as one correlated, attributable sequence rather than an anonymous sensor-wake. It changes display state only and never touches lock authority. A touch wake schedules NO re-sleep of its own and adds no timer: with absence detection off, the wake stands until the next boundary evaluates, which is the same pre-existing ruled behaviour sensor-wake already has; with absence detection on, run_occupancy remains the sole decider and clearing the absence stamp restarts the absence clock from the contact, so the panel stays lit for at least WALL_ABSENCE_TIMEOUT_MIN before absence can be re-established. The witness asserts no presence and writes no presence file. Re-sleep by suspend inside the window remains possible on an absence-enabled panel, and once it happens touch wake is gone by the Owner ruling of 2026-09-15 until the RTC alarm or the rocker returns - wall-touch-filter-sleep pre stops the filter daemon before suspend, destroying the virtual node - so the witness must survive the node's disappearance and re-resolve after resume and must never treat no node as a fault.

Title: Measured hardware-wake facts of record for the touchscreen
Detail: The claim that the internal I2C-HID touchscreen cannot wake the machine from S3 is measured once and recorded with its date, rather than inherited as belief. A read-only report script records /proc/acpi/wakeup with every device and its enabled or disabled state (especially the XHC and PCIe-port rows wall-wakeprep.sh re-arms), the touchscreen's power/wakeup resolved by identity by walking from the matching input node to the ancestor that carries the flag, and /sys/power/mem_sleep and /sys/power/state so the sleep state the panel actually enters is on the record beside the wakeup flags. The script writes nothing, enables nothing and suspends nothing: the Owner ruling of 2026-09-15 keeps suspend at the lowest power, so a touchscreen that unexpectedly reads enabled and proves to work is new evidence for the coordinator and the Owner, not licence to change the ruling. Until a dated entry exists in WALL-BURN-IN.md the limitation is explicitly marked unmeasured.

Title: Grid debt planner

Title: Volume-request transport verdict isolation and instance collection
Detail: main distinguishes EOF before a request from an incomplete read: the former journals a no-op and succeeds, the latter fails. After read_request supplies a request, main returns the apply result even when writing its verdict raises BrokenPipeError; handle_request retains its existing empty-byte parse result. The service template uses CollectMode=inactive-or-failed so spent connection instances disappear from the manager list.

Title: Device-capability filesystem trim wrapper and unit override
Detail: The wrapper enumerates real mountpoints, keeps one operation per source and reads each source device's DISC-MAX before invoking stock fstrim options. A zero maximum prints a skip reason and is not an error; any fstrim failure after a non-zero capability is returned. Firstboot installs the wrapper and writes a fstrim.service drop-in whose empty ExecStart resets the inherited list before its replacement command.

Title: Firstboot VA-API HEVC profile probe
Detail: Firstboot tests vainfo output for the exact HEVC Main VLD profile. It logs the driver version only on that match, otherwise emits a conspicuous non-fatal black-frame warning; absence of vainfo is an explicit unrun result. IF-019 keeps the required Electron feature switches on the counterpart side of this image capability.

Title: Desktop S/PDIF external-source restart classification
Detail: wall-spdif-in alone is classified as an external-source forwarder: its capture clock is supplied by a sleeping desktop, so a reopen failure may be temporary. The sibling audio units remain outside this requirement because their sources are internal to the panel and no corresponding normal-absence evidence exists.

Title: Start-limit-safe geometric restart schedule
Detail: The unit uses RestartSec=2, RestartSteps=6 and RestartMaxDelaySec=120 with its existing Restart=always and 60-second/10-start start limit. The derived starts at 0, 2, 6, 14, 31 and 66 seconds keep the temporary-absence retry rate below the armed limit while retaining a bounded retry ceiling.

Title: Adapter re-add delegates switch policy
Detail: The adapter rule directly wants wall-line-in, wall-kiosk-loop, wall-spdif-in and wall-amp-trigger, but wants wall-audio-resume once rather than naming switch legs. The reused non-sticky resume unit invokes apply-state, whose ALL_LEGS is the sole owner of speaker, headset and microphone leg policy.

Title: Absent adapter is a successful deferred apply
Detail: In bus mode apply-state resolves the configured adapter ALSA id from /proc/asound/card*/id before applying. If absent it journals a deferred apply, writes its boot stamp when applicable, and exits zero without issuing mixer or systemctl commands; a present adapter continues through normal counted failure handling.

Title: Relay alias and independent actuator ordering
Detail: The CH340 rule supplies TAG+=systemd and SYSTEMD_ALIAS=/dev/wall_amp_relay on every non-remove event and add-only SYSTEMD_WANTS for the actuator. wall-amp-trigger Wants and orders After the alias but does not BindsTo it, so relay absence cannot stop the audio detector while its bounded node wait and reopen logic retain recovery.

Title: Audio-mode absent-adapter deferred selection
Detail: Before stopping clients or touching mixers, wall-audio-mode resolves the configured ALSA card id under /proc/asound. If absent, it writes the requested mode file and matching output-chain symlink through one checked helper, logs that legs are deferred and exits zero. A selection that cannot be published is NOT a deferral: the helper rolls the symlink back to the previous mode and the command exits non-zero, and a rollback that itself fails is reported distinctly as an inconsistent selection rather than as a clean refusal, with that distinction carried in the exit status and not only in the log. A link path that exists but is not a readable symlink is refused before any mutation, because no rollback could restore it. The ordinary branch retains its counted operation failures and non-zero exit, because that branch may have stopped one graph and failed to establish the next.

Title: Firstboot preserves the audio-mode failure boundary
Detail: Firstboot continues to fail_step on a non-zero wall-audio-mode result and names its half-application hazard. The mode command itself makes the removable-adapter classification, so firstboot does not pattern-match error text or convert any other audio provisioning failure into success.

Title: Amp daemon clean dependency-stop exit
Detail: After SIGTERM or SIGINT, the daemon attempts its existing safe relay shutdown and records the result. It returns zero only when the relay device node is absent, because there is then no contact to open and the re-add recovers it; a PRESENT relay that refuses its OFF still returns non-zero, since the amplifier may remain energized. The process exit carries that result rather than discarding it. Its configuration validation and pre-loop unsafe-start result remain non-zero, so only a requested lifecycle stop is reclassified.

Title: Merged-bus capture adapter and the bus-mode gate
Detail: One restartable `arecord` child reads `bus_monitor` at the shape asound-bus-mode.conf fixes -- S16_LE, 48000 Hz, two channels, 1024-frame periods -- using the raw-pipe pattern the amplifier detector already proved on this panel, so an ALSA open failure kills a child rather than the service and is reported from the child's own stderr instead of being silent. The PCM is opened only while /etc/wall-panel/audio-mode reads `bus`; the other three configurations do not declare `bus_monitor` at all, so they are answered with an explicit unavailable state and no device is touched. The mode is re-read on every block, so a live `wall-audio-mode` change is answered rather than leaving a stale document. A capture that would not open is likewise unavailable and never reuses a prior loud block, and every reopen bumps the capture generation so a consumer can tell a different capture from a gap in this one. The window handed to the transform is two periods, decimated by four behind a four-tap boxcar whose first null sits exactly at the decimated Nyquist, because one period is barely one cycle of the lowest band and picking every fourth sample would fold audible energy into a labelled band.

Title: The derived bus document, its dB curve and its freshness fence
CodeSymbol: bus_source.build_document; bus_source.scalar_from_amplitude; bus_source.band_centres; visualizer.analyze_samples; visualizer.VisualizerTelemetry; panel-bus-visualizer.publish_document
Detail: The producer atomically replaces /run/wall-bus-visualizer/bus-telemetry.json with a bounded schema-2 document named `bus_monitor`, carrying finite normalized RMS, peak and exactly as many bands as there are published centres, an activity boolean, the capture generation and the producer's own monotonic observation instant. GENERATION IS TWO FACTS AT TWO LAYERS AND THEY ARE NEVER COLLAPSED: this document's `generation` is the CAPTURE generation, bumped on every reopen, and it exists so a consumer can tell a different capture from a gap in this one; the IF-015 `generation` the renderer validates for monotonicity is minted by the BROKER and is a property of the request epoch. Neither is derived from or surfaced through the other, and a reader who merges them loses the ability to distinguish a restarted capture from a restarted broker. The measurement and the presentation are separated deliberately: analyze_samples returns linear magnitudes, which is what a measurement honestly is, and the dB curve that makes a magnitude legible on a wall is applied by the producer -- the same curve the amplifier detector's readout uses, held to it by a test that imports both because the two processes cannot import each other. Band centres are named in Hz rather than left on the transform's default linear bin spacing, which would put every musical frequency in the first bin; no centre may exceed the decimated window's Nyquist, so a band never reports something folded down into its label. A producer that is not measuring publishes zeros and its reason, never the last frame it saw, because a frozen visualizer is indistinguishable from a quiet room. Publication failure is logged and survived: the document is a decoration and nothing about the capture, the routing or the relay depends on it. The document contains no samples, no microphone field, no device identity and no path.

Title: The broker's telemetry answer: the bus, the confirmed switch, and no microphone
Detail: The backend reads the bus document alone and validates its schema, source, producer state, bounds and freshness; a version-1 `speaker_tap` document is refused outright, because a post-switch level drawn under a label claiming the merged bus looks exactly like a working visualizer while quietly restoring the Headset blind spot. The producer's own three-valued state is believed rather than re-derived: unavailable reaches the shell as absence so a panel outside bus mode falls through to Frame Media, silent reaches it as a measured quiet room, and a stale document is silence rather than the last frame. Because `bus_monitor` is upstream of the switch it carries samples during Mute, so the activity claim -- and only the activity claim -- is ANDed with the confirmed output selection from the applier's state file, normalized exactly as the applier normalizes it so the answer is about the position the applier would act on. An unreadable state file is not audible: we cannot confirm it is audible is not a claim that it is. Levels are still reported under Mute, because what the bus carries is true regardless of where the switch sends it. The microphone may never stand in for the bus: the backend used to answer available with a fabricated silent bus whenever the microphone had telemetry and the bus had none, promoting a microphone reading into the bus's place, and that substitution is deleted. An absent, malformed or unavailable bus reports unavailable whatever the microphone is doing. The optional microphone block itself REMAINS, because it is not a visualizer feed: it is the level ring on the microphone button in the audio chrome, a different consumer with a different question, and it contributes no band, no rms, no peak and no activity claim. The two producers keep different staleness windows, because one window for both would either call the canceller stale constantly or leave a frozen bus readout on the wall.

Title: The frozen binary PCM frame codec
CodeSymbol: pcm_frame.encode_pcm_frame; pcm_frame.decode_pcm_frame; pcm_frame.decode_pcm_header; pcm_frame.PcmFrameError; pcm_frame.PCM_MAGIC; pcm_frame.PCM_VERSION; pcm_frame.MAX_PCM_FRAME_BYTES; bus_source.split_frames
Detail: One module is the sole encoder and decoder of IF-020's frozen little-endian WPCM version-1 frame. The header is fixed width so a reader can size a frame before it has the payload, which is what makes refusing an oversized claim a decision taken before the allocation rather than a failure discovered during it; header_bytes is carried in the frame and checked against the constant, so a future version that grows the header cannot be misparsed by an old reader as a corrupt version-1 frame. Every fixed field and the cross-field payload calculation are validated before any payload is returned, and a malformed, truncated, over-long or mislabelled frame raises rather than returning a partial one. A stream is split on whole frames only; a header that will not decode is not swallowed, because a stream that has lost frame alignment cannot be resynchronised by guessing and the only correct response is to drop the connection. The identical implementation in OfficeWallNaglight cannot import this one, so the two are held together by a byte-identical fixture shipped in both repositories and decoded by both suites.

Title: PCM endpoint authorization: peer credential and filesystem permission
Detail: The optional endpoint is AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM at /run/wall-bus-visualizer/pcm.sock, owned root and the panel group at mode 0660, and it is permissioned BEFORE it is listened on so nothing can connect in the window between bind and chmod. Every accepted connection is checked against SO_PEERCRED and a configured allow-list of uids; a denied peer is closed having received no frame, and the refusal is counted rather than described, because naming the peer would put an identity into a journal that exists to carry lifecycle. An EMPTY allow-list denies rather than permits, so a missing line in a unit file cannot become an open socket, and a non-integer or negative uid is denied. No client is started by default and at most two may attach, which is the Electron host plus the one that has not finished going away. Two facts the kernel vouches for are the right-sized authorization for the Owner's stated threat model -- make checking items off NagLight easy, keep children from checking things off for fun -- and are not presented as a defence against a compromised host, a hostile local process or a compromised home network.

Title: Depth-one PCM backpressure and the stream teardown lifecycle
Detail: Each authorized client owns one slot. Offering a block overwrites whatever was unsent and counts the drop; there is no buffer to bound, no high-water mark to tune and no drain policy, because a queue of audio that could grow is a recording held in memory and stale audio is worthless to a visualizer anyway. A slow client is given a bounded write deadline and then dropped, so it can delay neither the capture nor the telemetry every other process depends on. With nobody attached no frame is encoded at all, so the default configuration's cost is a comparison against zero and raw samples are never materialised into a second buffer nobody asked for. Disconnect, write failure, an unframeable block, a mode change, a capture failure, the capture ending and service stop all run one teardown function rather than five copies of it: the buffer is cleared first, then the connection is shut down and closed, and the unavailable document is published. That single function is what makes discard the buffers a statement a reader can check instead of infer.

Title: Visualizer failure isolation from routing and the amplifier relay
Detail: The visualizer service is observational. It opens one capture, writes its own runtime directory and binds one local socket, and it starts, stops and configures nothing else; its unit restricts address families to AF_UNIX, so there is no family present that could carry a sample off the machine. A capture failure, an analysis refusal, a telemetry write failure, a socket that will not bind and a client write failure are each logged within this service and none of them can change output routing, the applier's state, the speaker or headset legs, or the relay. The amplifier detector continues to open `speaker_tap` and only `speaker_tap`, never reads the new document, and takes the same relay decision whether this service is running, degraded or absent -- which is proved from the shipped text of both files and by injecting each failure, not asserted.

Title: The service's sandbox, payload, file modes and health probe
Detail: wall-bus-visualizer.service runs /usr/local/lib/wall-panel/panel-bus-visualizer.py with no User=, taking `bus_monitor` access through SupplementaryGroups=audio alone -- the pattern wall-bus-speaker and wall-amp-trigger already use, because ipc_gid 29 on the dsnoop means the group IS the privilege, and because `panel` is deliberately not that identity: the broker the renderer talks to must stay unable to open a sound device. Its ExecCondition keeps it out of the failure list in the three modes with no such PCM. Firstboot installs the daemon at 0755 and its three imports -- bus_source.py, pcm_frame.py and visualizer.py -- beside it at 0644, from the panel-audio tree that is each one's single home, exactly the way the root applier is installed beside wall_audio_state.py; the unit lands at 0644 in /etc/systemd/system and the unit is enabled and started, with every branch a warning rather than a failed step because a panel with no visualizer is a panel that shows Frame Media. The runtime directory is 0755 so the broker can traverse it, the document is chmod 0644 because the broker runs as `panel` and must read it, and the socket is 0660 root and the panel group. The health probe is `--check`: it verifies the tools and the configured user and reports the mode without opening a device or writing a file, because a probe that required a PCM client would call a healthy service broken every time nobody was looking at ProjectM.

Title: Bus mode's second reader of bus_monitor
Detail: asound-bus-mode.conf continues to declare `bus_monitor` as a dsnoop over the loopback capture slave at ipc_key 8822 with ipc_perm 0660, ipc_gid 29, S16_LE, 48000 Hz, two channels, period_size 1024 and buffer_size 8192, and no other shipped ALSA configuration declares it. Its comment no longer calls it the single reader of the bus: there are two, the leg the switch has started and the visualizer source, and a second reader is exactly what dsnoop exists for, so the plugin itself needed no change. The comment also records the distinction that a reader of this file most needs: the visualizer is PRE-switch and the amplifier detector is not, because the detector reads `speaker_tap` further down and must see only the Speaker leg. The visualizer's bus-mode gate is therefore a fact about this configuration rather than a fallback capture path, and no substitute PCM is offered in the other three modes.

Title: Mesh VPN carriage is opt-in and outside the offline ISO closure
Detail: The daemon is NOT in the distribution's base archive and is installed from the vendor's signed APT repository, so it CANNOT be baked into the offline ISO payload the way every core image is. This follows SN-016's precedent exactly rather than inventing a second rule: carriage is opt-in behind a knob, the install runs over SSH against a box that already has connectivity, and the reimage checklist names re-install and re-authorisation as manual steps that do not survive a reimage. The setup script is idempotent and non-interactive up to the authorisation step, which is interactive BY DESIGN — it prints the authorisation URL and stops. No reusable auth key is accepted by this script, written to the repo, baked into a payload or placed in the secret store, because a long-lived key that enrols nodes is a credential that admits devices to the whole LAN and it would be the one credential in this repo whose leak needs no other access to exploit.

Title: Forwarding sysctls live in a dedicated drop-in that additively survives
Detail: A subnet router must forward, so net.ipv4.ip_forward and net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding are set in their OWN file under /etc/sysctl.d rather than appended to an existing one, so the setting is greppable, removable with the feature, and cannot be silently reverted by a distribution upgrade rewriting a shared file. The drop-in's name sorts late deliberately so a lower-numbered file cannot win. This is a plain sysctl file and NOT a systemd drop-in: the accumulate-versus-replace rule that governs systemd list-valued directives does not apply here, last-write-wins does, and conflating the two is how an override that appears present ends up doing nothing.

Title: Route advertisement without exit-node duty and without DNS capture
Detail: Bring-up advertises the LAN CIDR as a subnet route and does NOT offer an exit node, so household internet traffic never transits the hub. It disables acceptance of the tunnel's DNS, because Technitium is this LAN's resolver and an injected resolver on the hub would displace the split-horizon records that make every service name resolve to the LAN address — the same split-horizon whose absence, through a different consumer, already produced a permanently unhealthy container that was working correctly. The advertised CIDR is read from the same deploy knob that feeds LAN_CIDR rather than being written twice, because two literals for one subnet is how they diverge. Route approval is a console-side action the script cannot perform and must not claim: the script reports the route as advertised-pending-approval and says so, never as active.

Title: The tunnel CIDR joins the existing address gate rather than adding a second one
Detail: LAN_CIDR gains the tunnel's CIDR beside the LAN's, so a tunnel client is admitted by the SAME remote_ip rule that admits a LAN client and no second mechanism exists to drift from it. The matcher stays remote_ip and NEVER client_ip, because client_ip trusts X-Forwarded-For and would hand the allow-list to anyone willing to forge a header. The gate must continue to exclude the docker bridge range: LAN_CIDR was once Caddy's private_ranges, which includes the bridge space, which put the one deliberately public workload inside the LAN gate — so a change to this value is asserted by test against both the admit and the exclude, not merely eyeballed. When the tunnel CIDR changes, this value and the daemon's advertisement change together in one edit or LAN clients are unaffected while tunnel clients receive 403 with correct credentials, which presents as an authentication fault and is not one.

Title: Gateway provenance: named upstream, pinned digest, and NOT the upstream installer
Detail: THE UPSTREAM IS NAMED AND SO IS ITS REGISTRY: FreeLLMAPI by Neu Software LLC, ghcr.io/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi, and no fork, mirror or other namespace may be referenced - any other path FAILS rather than warns. THE FORK HAZARD IS THE REASON THIS ROW NAMES THE PATH AT ALL, and it is not hypothetical: this project has thousands of forks, a search for it returns forks ranked ABOVE the original, and an earlier pass of this very work misread a fork's zero-star counters as the project's and its correct pointer to the author's own registry as a third party's. Anyone pinning a digest here should assume they are looking at a fork until they have checked the author, and the authoritative pointer is the project site, which names the canonical repository directly. THE UPSTREAM INSTALL SCRIPT IS NOT USED. Upstream's quickstart is a piped curl-to-shell installer that writes a directory, generates configuration and starts a container; convenient, and the opposite of every property this stack requires - it is unpinned, it executes remote code as root at deploy time, and it produces a deployment no commit describes. The service is deployed by THIS repo's compose with a digest recorded in gateway-image.pin together with the version and date it corresponds to, so an upgrade is a reviewable commit rather than a re-run of a script whose content may have changed. The image is pinned BY DIGEST; a floating tag fails the check outright, because this service holds every provider credential and an auto-updated credential concentrator is precisely the failure the pin exists to prevent. The service is profile-gated and absent from the default profile; it publishes NO host port, staying on the docker bridge behind the existing Caddy; provider credentials and the encryption key arrive through the existing secret materialisation as an env file and are never written into the committed compose file. Upstream states the project is local-first and single-user and advises against exposing it publicly, which is consistent with reaching it only from the LAN and the tunnel and is recorded here so a later reader does not mistake the Caddy gate for an invitation to widen it.

Title: The gateway's own bearer key is required including on the LAN
Detail: Every request carries the gateway's own bearer key, and an absent or wrong key is refused before any provider is contacted. THE LAN IS NOT EXEMPT, and that is a deliberate departure from how this stack gates its other LAN services: the ambient LAN trust the rest of the stack relies on is not sufficient for the one origin that fronts every provider credential the household holds. The key is distinct from every provider credential and from ai-cli's, so revoking it costs no provider access and a leak of one does not imply the others.

Title: The gateway and the AI CLI lane stay separate and the older posture is unchanged
Detail: The gateway's README states its wider-reach departure explicitly, the way the AI CLI block's did, so the reason this service is reachable off-box is recorded where the next reader will find it rather than inferred from the compose file. ai-cli's bind to loopback or a docker bridge address is UNCHANGED and is asserted by test in this change, not assumed: the whole risk of adding a second, deliberately wider lane is that the first one is quietly relaxed to match. No gateway route names an ai-cli endpoint, and the two share no credential, account or volume.

Title: Two probe layers, five states, and the deadline that bounds the only guess
Detail: THE STATE IS DECIDED BY TWO SEPARATE LAYERS AND CONFLATING THEM IS THE DEFECT THIS ROW EXISTS TO PREVENT. Layer one is REACHABILITY: ICMP and a TCP connect to the inference port. Neither answering - including a TCP connect that TIMES OUT or is REFUSED - is `off`. Either answering is `up`. A reachability timeout is NEVER `up`: a powered-off or partitioned box times out, and reporting it up would suppress the wake that is the whole point. Layer two is READINESS and it runs ONLY on a host that layer one already found reachable: a model listing that returns success AND names the target model as loaded is `ready`; a listing that returns success without the target model, returns an error, or TIMES OUT leaves the state at `up`, because the box is demonstrably answering and the model is merely not servable yet - which is the ordinary condition for tens of seconds after a wake while weights load into VRAM. PRECEDENCE WHEN THE LAYERS DISAGREE IS FIXED AND ORDERED: an expired wake deadline yields `failed` and outranks everything, because a wake that did not happen must not be masked by a stale probe; then layer one, because an unreachable host cannot be ready whatever a cached listing said; then layer two. `waking` is the ONLY estimated state, is entered solely by firing a wake, and carries a bounded deadline after which it becomes `failed` - it is structurally incapable of persisting, because a state that can stay waking forever never tells a caller to stop waiting. No input is reduced to a truthiness check over a merged result.

Title: Wake actuation sits behind a provider seam because the shipped provider is unproven
Detail: Actuation is an interface with the magic-packet implementation as ONE provider, selected by configuration. The target is the PHYSICAL adapter's MAC from a deploy knob — not resolved from the host's IP, which on this box returns the vEthernet adapter's address and would silently wake nothing, because the physical NIC is bound to a Hyper-V external vSwitch and the host's LAN address does not live on it. The provider is fire-and-forget with no acknowledgement, so the only evidence of success is the readiness probe subsequently answering, which is why the deadline is mandatory and why one wake is fired per attempt rather than per retry. A second provider — switched mains with firmware restore-on-power-loss — must be addable without touching the state machine, because the magic-packet path through this vSwitch is UNVERIFIED as of 2026-09-18 and may never work on this hardware.

Title: Holding a request beats returning an error
Detail: A request for a local model arriving while the state is not ready is HELD to a bounded cap with the wake fired in parallel, and on expiry falls through to a configured non-local provider rather than returning an error. Coding agents and chat clients handle a slow answer far better than a 503 with Retry-After, and the free-tier fallback is always available because no local-only routing constraint was imposed. The wake fires ONCE for the hold, not once per internal retry, or a burst of held requests becomes a burst of magic packets. A caller may therefore observe a multi-second time-to-first-byte against a cold box; that is this path working, and it is stated in the interface so a consumer does not treat it as a hang.

Title: The hub decides sleep; the dev PC actuates it, by polling
Detail: AN EARLIER SET OF ROWS CONTRADICTED ITSELF HERE AND THE CONTRADICTION SURVIVED SEVERAL REVIEWS. One row gave the hub an idle timer that returns the box to sleep; this row and IF-022 said sleep actuation was the dev PC's own and explicitly not a remote command. Both cannot be true, and as written NEITHER SIDE COULD APPLY BOTH REQUIRED CONDITIONS: the hub alone knows the local-model request history and consumes the session signal, while the dev PC alone can suspend itself. THE SPLIT IS NOW EXPLICIT. The hub owns POLICY: it decides sleep is permissible only when the idle period has elapsed with no local-model request AND the session signal says detached, failing closed to attached per LLR-978. It publishes that verdict and does nothing else. The dev PC owns ACTUATION: it POLLS that verdict (IF-026) and suspends itself. Polling rather than receiving is deliberate and consistent with this site's posture - it opens no inbound endpoint on the dev PC, so the sleep path adds no listener and no credential to a machine that already carries the remote-desktop service. THE RACE THE ORIGINAL WORDING FEARED IS STILL ANSWERED, and better: because the dev PC actuates, it re-checks its OWN in-flight state immediately before suspending and declines if work is running. A remote command could not have done that - it would have arrived, been correct when sent, and been wrong on arrival. The verdict is advisory and one-directional: it can permit a sleep the dev PC then chooses to take, and it can never compel one.

Title: The state is observable where an operator already looks
Detail: The state is served over HTTP for the gateway, published to the existing broker for anything else, and probed by the existing uptime monitor — no new observability surface is introduced. The monitor is what makes a rotted wake path discoverable BEFORE a request discovers it, which matters because the wake path's only failure mode is silence and the hardware binding beneath it is unverified. Every published document carries the instant the state was determined, so a stale document is distinguishable from a current one rather than being read as fresh.

Title: One volume, two processes, and the key pair that proves it
Detail: The rendezvous and relay processes are two services sharing exactly ONE named volume, declared once, because two volumes silently produce two key pairs and a client that reaches the rendezvous but never the relay — a failure that presents as an intermittent connection rather than as a misconfiguration. Host networking carries the documented TCP and UDP ports. The generated public key is recorded as a deployment output and required of every client: a server reachable without it admits any caller who can reach it. The volume joins the LOCAL backup set and not the offsite one, because the key pair is not reproducible from the repo and re-generating it invalidates every installed client.

Title: LAN and tunnel only, enforced where a HOST socket is actually filtered
Detail: The remote-desktop ports are admitted from the LAN CIDR and the tunnel CIDR and rejected otherwise, enforced in the INPUT chain for IPv4 AND in the ip6tables INPUT chain for IPv6, and explicitly NOT in DOCKER-USER. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE CHOICE FROM THE FAIL2BAN JAIL AND IT IS THE CORRECT ONE HERE, for the reason game-isolation.sh already records next door: DOCKER-USER is consulted for traffic that is ROUTED to a published container port, and these services run with host networking, so their sockets are HOST sockets and that traffic is delivered locally through INPUT without ever entering DOCKER-USER. A DOCKER-USER rule here would be visibly present, would pass a naive review, and would filter nothing - the boundary would be open to any caller who could reach the host while the control reported itself installed. THE IPv6 HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL: a v4-only rule leaves the same listener reachable over v6 on any box that acquires a routable v6 address, which is exactly the outcome the mesh tunnel makes more likely rather than less. Both families are asserted by address, never by container name, because container names do not resolve across networks and a name-based probe passes for the wrong reason. No router forward is added for these ports under any circumstance; the remote path is the tunnel, which is affordable precisely because it needs no forward.

Title: Service mode is the requirement, not a preference
Detail: The Windows client is installed AS A SERVICE from an administrator account. A user-session or portable process dies at logout and goes blind at a UAC prompt, because the secure desktop is not in the user's session — so a machine woken to a sign-in screen would be unreachable in exactly the state remote access exists for. This is the SAME property the inference endpoint needs after a cold wake, and the README says so in both places on purpose: services, not sessions, is one fact that three separate goals depend on, and getting it wrong makes all three half-work and only after a cold wake. The unattended password is a distinct high-entropy secret and explicitly NOT the Owner's Windows password, so a leak of one does not hand over the other. Reaching a genuinely LOGGED-OUT machine's sign-in screen and entering the credential is hardware acceptance; a locked machine is a different state and proves nothing about this.

Title: Wake is single-flight with one linearization point and NO I/O under the lock
Detail: A wake is ONE operation keyed to the target host, not one per request, and a single lock establishes the linearization point. WHAT HAPPENS INSIDE THAT LOCK IS STRICTLY BOUNDED, because the previous draft of this row required resolution inside the critical section and that is two bugs waiting. (a) RE-ENTRANCY: resolving a flight while holding the lock runs waiter continuations synchronously, and a continuation that reads state or requests another wake re-enters the same lock and DEADLOCKS the service. (b) UNBOUNDED HOLD: firing a magic packet, probing reachability or readiness, publishing to the broker and serving HTTP are all I/O, and performing any of them under the lock turns a bounded critical section into a lock wait as long as the slowest network operation - so one blocked probe stalls every joiner and every state read, including the health endpoint that would tell an operator why. THE RULE IS THEREFORE EXPLICIT: under the lock, and only under the lock, read the current state, join or start a flight, publish the terminal state, detach and remove the flight, and SNAPSHOT the waiter list. Release the lock. THEN notify the snapshotted waiters and perform every piece of I/O. Publication and removal still happen together so no arrival can interleave between them, which is what finding 3 of the prior round required and is preserved intact. THE FLIGHT OWNS THE DEADLINE: joiners neither extend, restart nor replace it, because a deadline any newcomer can refresh never expires under load, reintroducing the unbounded `waking` LLR-966 forbids; a late joiner inherits the remaining time. A flight resolves ONCE and every snapshotted waiter observes the same terminal outcome. On failure it resolves to `failed` and is cleared in the same critical section, so a subsequent request starts a NEW flight rather than joining a dead one.

Title: The policy reference is a document, and the check does not pretend otherwise
Detail: TAILSCALE POLICY LIVES SERVER-SIDE. The coordination service holds it, the daemon fetches it from there, and tailscaled never reads local disk for it - verified on the running hub 2026-09-18: nothing under /var/lib/tailscale, no unit file and no open file descriptor references the artifact. So a tracked policy file is a DOCUMENT TO PASTE INTO THE CONSOLE and nothing more, and this row previously claimed otherwise. An earlier version deployed it to the hub and had --check-only FAIL when it was absent or looked permissive. THAT CHECK WAS BACKWARDS AND IS REMOVED: it confirmed that a file this repo wrote said what this repo wrote in it, which is true whatever policy the tailnet is actually running - and it is false-green in the only case that matters, a wide-open policy applied in the console while the tracked file sits there looking correct. Verifying the policy in force needs a tailnet API key; that key can rewrite who reaches the entire LAN, and carrying one on the hub to catch the Owner's own console edits costs more than it saves under the standing threat model (ruled 2026-08-09, restated 2026-09-18). THE REFERENCE ALSO HAS TO BE RIGHT, and the first one was not, in two ways worth keeping: it placed an autogroup inside a `groups` entry, where members must be full email addresses, which the console rejects outright; and every rule targeted a tag while the hub authenticates AS A USER and carries no tag, so with deny-by-omission the policy accepted nothing and applying it would have cut off tunnel access to the hub. Both are asserted against the reference now. WHAT THE CHECK STILL DOES: it queries tailnet-lock state and WARNS when disabled, because that risk is a compromised coordinator or identity account - external, worth knowing, not worth refusing to converge over. The identity account's multi-factor property cannot be observed from this box and is not claimed; it is an operator attestation. AND THE URGENCY IS SCALED TO THE TAILNET: on a single-user tailnet the default policy means the Owner's own devices reach the Owner's own devices, which is fine. A policy starts mattering when a second person, a shared node or a tagged service appears.

Title: The fence is installed before the listeners and replays idempotently
Detail: The rules are installed by a unit ordered BEFORE and required by the owning service, so a failure to program either address family stops the listeners rather than leaving them unrestricted; this is the ordering the crossplay relay's own isolation unit already uses after its first version got it wrong and re-opened the window on every boot. The installer is IDEMPOTENT BY MARKER in both families: it removes its own prior rules before installing the current set, so a replay after a reboot converges rather than accumulating duplicates and a changed CIDR does not leave the older, wider rule behind. SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY. These ports are not forwarded at the router and this site has no inbound path from the internet at all, so this fence is a boundary against other devices on the home network, not against a determined attacker. Per the Owner's standing threat model it is NOT extended with reload hooks, watchdog timers or service-stop cascades to cover a hostile local actor flushing the ruleset - that scenario is explicitly out of scope, and the machinery it would require is not carried. Verification is that a connection from a source outside the LAN and tunnel ranges is refused on each documented TCP and UDP port.

Title: One owner starts the listeners
Detail: Both containers declare `restart: "no"`, so the container runtime never starts them on its own - not at boot, not after a daemon restart, not after a crash - and they are started only by homehub-rustdesk.service, which `Requires=` and is `After=` the isolation unit. A failure to program the fence therefore stops the listeners existing rather than losing a race to them. This is the ownership model the crossplay relay next door already uses, reused rather than reinvented. A deliberate manual compose start by the Owner is not defended against: it is the Owner's own machine and their own command, and per the standing threat model this row does not carry a mechanism to prevent it. The property that matters is that nothing starts these containers WITHOUT someone deciding to.

Title: The sleep inhibit needs an authoritative session signal, and it fails closed
Detail: LLR-969 requires the idle timer to be inhibited while an interactive remote-desktop session is attached and never said HOW that is known, which left the most damaging failure in this whole design undefined. THE SIGNAL IS AN EXPLICIT INTERFACE (IF-025) with a named source, a poll interval and a STALENESS BOUND: a reading older than that bound is not a reading. FAIL CLOSED MEANS ATTACHED. An absent, stale, malformed or unauthenticated session signal is treated as SESSION ATTACHED and the box is NOT slept. This direction is the whole point and the opposite of the usual instinct: the cost of a false 'attached' is that a machine stays awake and burns a few watts until the next reading; the cost of a false 'detached' is the machine sleeping under the Owner's hands mid-session, which SN-044 names as worse than never sleeping at all. A relay that reports a disconnected session as still attached therefore costs nothing this design cares about, while the reverse loses work. The inhibit is not the only condition - the idle period must also have elapsed with no local-model request - and an explicit operator override may force sleep, which is the one path permitted to ignore an attached session because a human is asserting the truth the signal cannot.
